mechanisms.savepoints: Persistent burn bound to backend/transaction plus non-rollback session advisory guard; explicit held-lock check because advisory locks are reentrant.
mechanisms.known_lock_waits: EXCLUSIVE table lock and row/policy locks with NOWAIT acquired before final local time check; busy attempts remain burned.
mechanisms.bypass_controls: Caller has EXECUTE only; legacy gate and admin fault variant denied; advisory APIs revoked for caller in the private lab; qualified pg_catalog.pg_locks and pg_temp last.
mechanisms.scope: Experimental one-row UPDATE only; no production integration or change to R1 contracts.

limitations: Session advisory state is ephemeral, not a durable ledger; old context rejection after restart relies on the separate burn and backend/transaction binding.
Fresh private lab revokes PUBLIC advisory API privileges; deploying those ACL changes in an existing server is not authorized or recommended by these results.
The internal NOLOGIN gate role required table-level UPDATE for LOCK TABLE; caller still has no direct DML or role membership.
Known relation/tuple waits are removed, not all possible scheduling, buffer, WAL, I/O or internal waits after the clock check.
The residual expiry counterexample was produced by a separate admin-only fault-injection variant, not observed in the unmodified corrected function.
No remote revocation authority, authenticated UTC uncertainty, power-loss storage failure, historical recovery or concurrent live clone was validated.
Historical rollback, clone identities and loss of external continuity remain blockers.
Current SQL/catalog/single-transaction protected contracts do not admit this lab schema/control path automatically.
GAP-001/002 remain open; AUTH-03/F02/G2/G4 remain unchanged and closed.
development_note: An initial run failed on LOCK TABLE privilege requirements; its private resources were cleaned. The subsequent privilege correction and temp-schema hardening were exercised in fresh clusters.
